name: Make balloon animals
blurb: Five or six twists cover most designs, and a dog, a sword and a flower will make you the most popular adult at any children’s party.
gear: 260Q modelling balloons — the long thin ones
A balloon pump, not your lungs
steps: Learn to inflate correctly with a pump, leaving an uninflated tail of several centimetres for the air to expand into.
Learn the basic twist, and always hold every twist you have made — they unwind the instant you let go.
Learn the lock twist and the ear twist, which secure the sequence so you can let go safely.
Learn the dog, which uses only basic and lock twists, and which teaches the whole grammar.
Learn a sword and a flower — the two most requested designs after the dog.
Practise speed: at a party you need to make one in under a minute.
tips: Over-inflating is the main cause of popping. Leave that tail.
Never give balloons to very small children — uninflated and popped pieces are a serious choking hazard.
Latex allergies are common enough to ask about before handing balloons out.
proof: You make a dog, a sword and a flower, each in under a minute, without popping any.
